children: Strategy could be removed from MSCI's global equity indexes after the official adoption of a new set of rules.

MSCI said non-operating companies will be ineligible for its global investable market indexes as of the close of Nov. 30. Strategy is on MSCI's list of companies that could potentially be deleted from the indexes as a result of the change.
The index provider proposed the change in rules in August. The bitcoin treasury company Strategy opposed the changes in an Aug. 31 statement, saying that the proposal was "misguided."
The removal wouldn't have a meaningful impact on Strategy's business, executives from the company said in a letter to MSCI at the time.

MSCI defines non-operating companies as investment funds, business development companies and other passive investment vehicles, which are currently ineligible for inclusion on its indexes. Its new definition would also include other corporate issuers with similar characteristics, which it said it would identify through new quantitative screens.

An initial screen would determine whether an issuer is a company with substantial operating assets. If an issuer fails that screen, it would become ineligible for index inclusion if flagged on four or more of five financial ratios as part of another screen, MSCI said.
MSCI said it would publish a final list of affected current constituents on Nov. 11.
